source.corpus: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) kor sentences, CC BY 2.0 FR
source.note: 표현과 예문, 풀이는 Daily English가 직접 썼고(AI 도움), 빈도만 말뭉치에서 셌습니다.

items.exampleKo: I love you more than anything in the world.
items.tip: Casual form for your partner. The polite form is 사랑해요.

items.meaning: I like you. / I really like you.
items.exampleKo: I really like you.
items.tip: The most common way to confess feelings before dating.

items.exampleKo: I'm totally into you these days.

items.meaning: You mean a lot to me.
items.exampleKo: You mean so much to me.
items.tip: Works for close friends too.

items.exampleKo: Honestly, I'm into you.

items.meaning: It was love at first sight.
items.exampleKo: Actually, I fell for you at first sight.

items.meaning: I'm happy when I'm with you.
items.exampleKo: I'm always happy when I'm with you.

items.meaning: I'm so glad I met you.
items.exampleKo: I'm really glad I met you.
Babe, did you sleep well?
items.tip: A very common pet name between couples. 여보 is used by married couples.

items.exampleKo: Thanks for the coffee, you're the best!
items.tip: Also common between friends.

items.exampleKo: I still get butterflies when I'm with you.
items.tip: There's no exact English word. It's that excited, fluttery feeling.

items.meaning: I can't stop thinking about you.
items.exampleKo: I keep thinking about you today.
You're my everything.
items.tip: Very sweet, so save it for special moments.

items.exampleKo: See you tomorrow, kiss!
items.tip: A cute word for a light kiss. Couples also type 쪽.

items.exampleKo: Good night, sweet dreams.
Your sleeping face is so cute.

items.meaning: Do you want to go out with me?
items.exampleKo: Will you go out with me?
items.tip: Koreans often "confess" (고백) to officially start dating.

items.exampleKo: I miss you so much.
items.tip: Literally "I want to see you". It's how Koreans say "I miss you".

items.exampleKo: We just said goodbye and I already miss you.

items.meaning: I can't wait to see you!
items.exampleKo: Just three more days! I can't wait to see you!
I'm counting down the days until we meet.
items.tip: 손꼽아 means counting on your fingers.

items.example: 경치 진짜 예뻐. 네가 여기 있으면 좋겠다.
items.exampleKo: The view is so pretty. I wish you were here.
I was just thinking of you.
See you again! Get home safe.
This café feels empty without you.
items.tip: 허전하다 is the feeling that something is missing.

items.meaning: I want to hear your voice.
items.example: 전화할 수 있어? 목소리 듣고 싶어.
items.exampleKo: Can you call? I want to hear your voice.

items.meaning: I want to give you a big hug.
items.exampleKo: Rough day, right? I want to give you a big hug.
Even at work, you're all I think about.
I'll be waiting, come back soon.
Take your time, I'll wait.
When do we see each other next?
That's so funny lol
items.tip: ㅋ is the sound "k" from 크크 (laughing). More ㅋ = funnier.

items.exampleKo: Okay hehe
items.tip: Softer than ㅋㅋ. Adds a friendly, smiling tone.

items.exampleKo: Yeah, see you later
items.tip: From 응응. Very short, so it can feel a bit cold.

items.exampleKo: Chicken? Let's go!
items.tip: From 고고 (go go).

items.exampleKo: I'm so tired today T_T
items.tip: Looks like crying eyes. Also ㅜㅜ.

items.exampleKo: Nah, it's fine
items.tip: From 노노 (no no).

items.exampleKo: Thanks for helping!
items.tip: From 감사.

items.exampleKo: Sorry I'm late
items.tip: From 죄송. Only with close friends.

items.exampleKo: OK, see you at 7
What are you doing now?
Good job today, good night!
items.tip: A cute mix of English "good" and 밤 (night).

items.exampleKo: This is awesome!
items.tip: Used for both good surprises and shocking news.

items.exampleKo: OMG, really?
items.tip: A very common reaction to surprising news.

items.exampleKo: This is seriously delicious.
items.tip: Slang from English "real".

items.exampleKo: Seriously tired
items.tip: Short for 레알.

items.exampleKo: Congrats on passing!
items.tip: From 축하.

items.exampleKo: This movie is so much fun.
items.tip: 꿀 (honey) + 잼 (from 재미, fun). The opposite is 노잼.

items.exampleKo: Okay, I'll text you later.
What are you up to this weekend?

items.example: 오늘 하루 어땠어? 다 얘기해 줘.
items.exampleKo: How was your day? Tell me everything.
Nothing much, just resting at home.
Me too, I barely slept.
Just chilling with my cat.
No way! You met him?
You saw a celebrity? That's amazing!
Tell me about it, Mondays are the worst.
items.tip: Literally "my words". Means "exactly what I'm saying".

items.exampleKo: Guess what! I got in!
items.tip: Used to start a story or share news.

items.exampleKo: You're quiet today, what's wrong?
Did you eat? Don't skip meals.
items.tip: A very common Korean greeting that means "I care about you", not only about food.

items.exampleKo: Long time no see! How have you been?

items.meaning: Good job today. / You worked hard.
items.exampleKo: You worked hard today too.
items.tip: Said at the end of a long day. It means "thank you for your hard work".

items.exampleKo: Oh, I see.
That's fun, tell me more!
You're moving here? Really?
Work is the same as always.

items.meaning: What are you into these days?
items.exampleKo: What are you obsessed with lately?
You silly thing, I still love you.
items.tip: With a soft voice it's affectionate, not an insult.

items.exampleKo: Don't be mad, I'm just kidding.
Stop it, I'm embarrassed!
You want me to do it again? Dream on.
Nice try, I'm not falling for it.
Not funny. Give me back my phone.
Balloons for my birthday? You're so extra.
items.tip: 오버 comes from English "over" and means "too much".

items.exampleKo: Do what you want, you win.
items.tip: Can sound cold, so say it with a smile.

items.exampleKo: That's so mean! I tried my best.
Gotcha! Just kidding.
Busted! You ate my snacks, right?
I'm a bad cook? Says who?
You're impossible, stop laughing.

items.example: 한 번 이겼다고 잘난 척하지 마.
items.exampleKo: You won once, don't show off.

items.meaning: Just kidding! / That was a lie!
items.exampleKo: Kidding! You look great today.
Want chicken? Deal!
items.tip: From English "call", like accepting a bet.

items.exampleKo: What's my cutie doing?
items.tip: A cute nickname, half teasing.

items.example: 오늘 밤 시간 돼? 보고 싶어.
items.exampleKo: Are you free tonight? I miss you.
Want to grab food after work?
Friday at 7? It's a date.
Should I pick you up at 7?
What time works for you tomorrow?
Something came up, can we reschedule?
Sorry, something suddenly came up.
I'll be there in 10 minutes!
Where should we meet? In front of the station?
Let's go Dutch today.
items.tip: From English "Dutch pay". In Korea, couples often take turns paying instead.

items.exampleKo: Today it's my treat.
Want to watch a movie at my place this weekend?

items.meaning: Text me when you get home.
items.exampleKo: Let me know when you get home.
items.tip: Koreans say this a lot. It shows you care.

items.exampleKo: It's late, I'll take you home.

items.meaning: I had a great time today.
items.exampleKo: I had a really great time today, thank you.
That was fun! Let's go again!

items.meaning: Are we still on for today?
items.exampleKo: Are we still on for dinner tonight?
Hello? Can you hear me?
Sorry, you're breaking up.
Your screen froze for a second.
Can I call you after work?
I'm on the bus, I'll call you back later.
Let's video call before bed.
items.tip: Koreans often say 영통 for short.

items.example: 거기 지금 몇 시야? 나 때문에 깼어?
items.exampleKo: What time is it there? Did I wake you up?
It's late here, I'm going to sleep now.
The time difference is so hard.
Wait, you're on mute!

items.example: 카메라 켜 줘, 얼굴 보고 싶어.
items.exampleKo: Turn on your camera, I want to see your face.

items.meaning: I fell asleep on the call.
items.exampleKo: Sorry, I fell asleep on the call last night.
Long distance is hard, but it's okay because it's you.
items.tip: Often shortened to 장거리.

items.exampleKo: I'll stay up until you call.
No, you hang up first!
items.tip: A classic cute couple moment in Korea too.

items.exampleKo: Good night, let's talk again tomorrow.
Can you see me? It's really dark here.

items.meaning: I didn't mean it like that.
items.exampleKo: Sorry, I didn't mean it like that.

items.example: 오늘 밤에 얘기 좀 할래? 중요한 거야.
items.exampleKo: Can we talk tonight? It's important.

items.example: 화난 거 아니야, 잠깐 혼자 있고 싶어.
items.exampleKo: I'm not mad, I just need some time alone.
items.tip: It doesn't mean breaking up. It means "I need time".

items.exampleKo: Honestly, that really hurt me.
Let's not fight, I miss you.
Sorry, I said too much.
We're okay now, right?
I hate fighting, let's make up.
It's okay, I forgive you.

items.example: 잠깐, 나 그렇게 말 안 했어.
items.exampleKo: Wait, I didn't say that.
You're right, I was wrong.
Don't be mad, let me explain.

items.example: 너한테 화난 거 아니야, 그냥 피곤해.
items.exampleKo: I'm not mad at you, I'm just tired.
Let's start over.

items.example: 무슨 말인지 알아, 근데 난 생각이 달라.
items.exampleKo: I see your point, but I think differently.
items.tip: Good to say before you disagree.

items.exampleKo: Don't worry, we're all good now.
items.tip: 풀리다 means a bad feeling is "untied" or gone.

items.exampleKo: I'm really sorry I upset you.
Whatever happens, I'm here for you.

items.example: 내일 중요한 날이지? 넌 할 수 있어!
items.exampleKo: Big day tomorrow? You've got this!
You missed the bus? That must be annoying.
It's cold, so take care of yourself.
You worked hard, get some rest.
Get well soon! Drink lots of water.
Don't cry, everything will be okay.
You did it! I'm proud of you.
Exams are almost over, hang in there!
items.tip: 힘내 literally means "find your strength".

items.meaning: Do you want to talk about it?
items.exampleKo: You look down. Want to talk about it?
It's okay, you did your best.

items.example: 걱정 마, 난 언제나 네 편이야.
items.exampleKo: Don't worry, I'm always on your side.
Even if you're busy, don't overdo it.
It's late, so get home safe.
items.tip: A very common goodbye between friends and couples.

items.exampleKo: I believe in you, you'll do great.

items.meaning: Don't be so hard on yourself.
items.exampleKo: Don't blame yourself so much.

items.meaning: Let me know if you need anything.
items.exampleKo: If you need anything, just tell me.
That dress looks so pretty!
items.tip: For a man, say 멋있다 (you look cool/handsome).

items.exampleKo: You packed me lunch? That's so sweet.
Look at this puppy, so cute!
You started painting? I love that!
You passed? That's great!
Your story is killing me.
You got engaged? I'm as happy as if it were me!
Looks delicious! Did you make it yourself?
You ran 10 km? That's awesome!
You drew this? You're talented.
Your message really cheered me up.
I'm totally obsessed with this song.
A pink suitcase? That's so you.
Your outfit is so cool today!
A new job near the beach? I'm jealous!
You fixed it already? You're a genius!
This café is the best!
items.tip: 짱 means "the best" in casual speech.

items.exampleKo: What does that mean?
items.tip: Say it softly so it doesn't sound like you're arguing.

items.meaning: How do you say this in Korean?
items.exampleKo: How do you say this in Korean?
Sorry, can you say that again?

items.meaning: Could you speak a little slower?
items.example: 조금 천천히 말해 줄래? 다 알아듣고 싶어.
items.exampleKo: Could you speak a bit slower? I want to catch everything.
Is that just how it is in Korea?
Sorry, I'm still learning Korean.

items.example: 내가 맞게 말했어? 솔직하게 말해 줘.
items.exampleKo: Did I say it right? Be honest.
Correct me if I'm wrong, okay?
Is it okay to speak casually to your parents?
items.tip: 반말 is casual speech. Use 존댓말 (polite speech) with elders and people you just met.

items.exampleKo: In my country, we eat cake on birthdays.
items.tip: Koreans say 우리나라 (our country) for their own country.

items.meaning: Let me teach you some English.
items.example: 영어 좀 알려 줄게. "I miss you" 해 봐!
items.exampleKo: Let me teach you some English. Say "I miss you"!
You celebrate it in summer? That's so interesting.
What's this called in Korean?

items.example: 그 농담은 번역하면 느낌이 안 살아.
items.exampleKo: That joke loses its feel in translation.
Sorry, I didn't quite catch that.

items.meaning: I'm nervous to meet your parents.
items.example: 너희 부모님 뵙는 거 너무 긴장돼.
items.exampleKo: I'm so nervous about meeting your parents.
items.tip: 뵙다 is the humble word for meeting elders.

items.example: 그 말 처음 들어. 무슨 뜻이야?
items.exampleKo: I've never heard that before. What does it mean?
Hi! How have you been?
items.tip: Casual hello and goodbye. Polite form: 안녕하세요.

items.exampleKo: Good morning, did you sleep well?
Long time no see, how are you?
Work is so-so.
Thanks for helping.
You're welcome, it's nothing.
It's okay, don't worry about it.
items.tip: Used for "I'm fine", "no problem", and "no thanks".

items.exampleKo: Sorry I'm late.
See you, let's meet tomorrow.
It's late, so get home safe.
I'm home! I'm hungry.
Welcome back, how was your day?
I'm hungry, let's eat.
I'm sleepy, I'm going to bed.
I'm so tired today.
It's really hot today.
It's cold outside, so dress warm.
Nice weather, want to go for a walk?
It's raining, take an umbrella.
Wait a sec, I'll be right there.
What time is it now?
Where are you now?

items.meaning: What do you want to eat?
items.exampleKo: What do you want for dinner?
Anything's fine, you decide.
This tteokbokki is so good!
Got it, I'll text you later.

items.meaning: Please take care of me. / Nice to meet you.
items.exampleKo: Let's get along from now on.
items.tip: Used when meeting someone new or asking for a favor.

items.exampleKo: Sorry, I'll head out first.
Sleep well, see you tomorrow.

items.meaning: Cheer up! / You can do it!
items.exampleKo: Good luck on your exam!
Long time no see, you haven't changed at all.
I'm having coffee, you?
Enjoy your meal, eat a lot.

items.meaning: Thank you for the meal. (before eating)
items.exampleKo: Thank you for the food!
items.tip: Said before eating, to the person who cooked or paid.

items.meaning: Thank you for the meal. (after eating)
items.exampleKo: Thank you for the meal, it was delicious.
Always stay healthy.
Are you up already?
Oh no, I overslept!
Wash your face when you wake up.
Brush your teeth before bed.
I'll take a shower now.
Did you eat breakfast?
I take the subway to work.
I'll take the bus today.
I go to work at 8.
What time do you get off work?
Are you going to school tomorrow too?
What did you eat for lunch?
I have to work overtime today too.
I'm on my way home.
I'm making dinner now.
I have to do laundry on the weekend.
I cleaned my room.
I'm going grocery shopping at the mart.
I stay home on days off.
I watch dramas at night.
I listen to music on my way to work.
I work out after work.
I take a walk after dinner.
I'll go take a bath.
I'll get ready for bed now.
I have to wake up early tomorrow.
I stayed up all night again.
I go back to sleep on weekends.
I brought a packed lunch today.
I bought a triangle kimbap at the convenience store.
Tomorrow is my day off.
What do you do on weekends?
I'm always busy on weekdays.
I study Korean every day.
I always take this road.
I sometimes cook myself.
I'm working from home today.
Let's take a short break.
I look at my phone before bed.
I'm getting ready, so wait.

items.meaning: Where do you want to go?
items.exampleKo: Where do you want to go today?
items.tip: Casual. Polite: 어디 가고 싶으세요?

items.exampleKo: Anywhere is fine if I'm with you.
It's my treat today.
items.tip: 쏘다 literally means 'to shoot'; slang for treating someone.

items.exampleKo: Let's each pay for our own.
items.tip: Also common: 반반 내자 (half and half).

items.example: 오늘은 내가 샀으니까 다음엔 네가 사.
items.exampleKo: I paid today, so you get the next one.
Want to share this? It's a big portion.
items.tip: -ㄹ래? asks 'do you want to?' casually.

items.exampleKo: That looks good. Give me just one bite.
I'm hungry. Shall we go eat?

items.meaning: This place has a nice vibe.
items.exampleKo: This place has a nice vibe. Let's come often.
items.tip: 분위기 = atmosphere, vibe.

items.meaning: Want me to take your photo?
items.example: 저기 서 봐. 사진 찍어 줄까?
items.exampleKo: Stand over there. Want me to take your photo?
It's pretty here. Let's take one together.
I'm on my way. Wait a little.
items.tip: -는 중 = in the middle of doing.

items.meaning: Please wait for me a bit.
items.exampleKo: Sorry I'm late. Please wait for me a bit.
I'm almost there. Just five minutes.
Where should we meet tomorrow?
items.tip: -ㄹ까? = shall we?

items.meaning: Let's meet in front of the station.
items.exampleKo: Let's meet in front of the station at seven.
It's late. I'll walk you home.
I checked the map but I'm lost. Where are you?
Come this way. It's prettier here.

items.text: 사람 너무 많다. 다른 데 가자.
items.meaning: It's too crowded. Let's go somewhere else.
items.example: 주말이라 사람 너무 많다. 다른 데 가자.
items.exampleKo: It's the weekend, so it's too crowded. Let's go somewhere else.

items.meaning: My legs hurt. Let's rest a bit.
items.example: 많이 걸었더니 다리 아파. 좀 쉬자.
items.exampleKo: We walked a lot and my legs hurt. Let's rest a bit.

items.meaning: I'll be right back, just going to the restroom.
items.exampleKo: Hang on, I'm going to the restroom for a sec.
items.tip: 다녀오다 = go and come back; 좀 softens it.

items.exampleKo: That shop looks nice. Let's check it out.
items.tip: -아/어 보자 = let's try.

items.exampleKo: Does this hat suit me?
That color really suits you.
Want to grab a coffee after the walk?
items.tip: 한잔하다 = have a drink (coffee or alcohol).

items.meaning: Want to go see a movie?
items.exampleKo: Want to go see a movie this weekend?
The weather's nice. Let's go for a walk.
I really had fun today. Thank you.
items.tip: 재밌다 is short for 재미있다.

items.meaning: You have to go already? That's a shame.
items.example: 시간 진짜 빠르다. 벌써 가야 돼? 아쉽다.
items.exampleKo: Time flies. You have to go already? That's a shame.
This place is nice. Let's come again next time.
It's raining. Let's share my umbrella.
It's chilly at night. Cold, right? Wear this.
There's a seat. Sit here.
I'll come pick you up at the station.

items.meaning: Let me show you around today.
items.exampleKo: Let me show you around today. Follow me.
items.tip: 안내하다 = to guide.

items.example: 여기 기억나? 우리 처음 만난 데야.
items.exampleKo: Do you remember this place? It's where we first met.
I'm happy to meet you.
That news is sad.
I get lonely when I'm alone.
Horror movies are scary.
I'm embarrassed singing in front of people.
I'm frustrated that we lost.
I'm annoyed by the traffic.
I'm nervous about the interview.
What a relief that you're safe.
You startled me by showing up!
That attitude makes me furious.
I'm really happy right now.
That movie was moving.

items.meaning: I miss it. (a time or place)
items.exampleKo: This song makes me nostalgic.
I can't be bothered to cook today.
This class is boring.
I feel comfortable with you.
Something feels off.
I met a friend from high school.
She's my best friend.
Do you have a boyfriend?
It's been a year since I got together with my girlfriend.
I'm traveling with my family.
I want to introduce you to my parents.
Do you have siblings?
We get along well.
We're a good match.
He's a really sweet person.
You're a fun person.
That person is on my mind.
I trust you.
Mom is worried.
I fought with a friend yesterday.
You look low on energy today.
I have no motivation on Mondays.
I feel good today!
I feel bad today.
I cried watching the movie.
Let's go together next time.
Can we meet tomorrow?
How about the day after tomorrow?
Are you free next Saturday?
What are you doing this weekend?
I'm going to Korea next month.
Do you have plans on Friday?
I'm free that day.

items.example: 미안, 그날은 안 될 것 같아.
items.exampleKo: Sorry, I don't think I can that day.
What time works tomorrow?
Where should we meet tomorrow?
I'll wait at the station.
Sorry, I think I'll be 5 minutes late.
If you hurry, you'll make it.
I canceled the reservation.
I'm looking forward to next week's trip.
Let's go on a trip over summer break.
Let's go to the festival together!
Did you decide where to go?
I haven't decided yet.
Hmm, I'll think about it.
items.tip: Can also be a soft "no".

items.exampleKo: Anytime is fine, I'll adjust.
Not today, let's do it another time.
I'll text you again when I know the time.
When's your birthday?
Next week is our anniversary.
Let's celebrate you passing!
What gift do you want for your birthday?
Where are you going on summer break?
I spend Lunar New Year with family.
items.tip: One of the two biggest Korean holidays.

items.exampleKo: We eat songpyeon on Chuseok.
On Christmas, couples go on dates.
items.tip: In Korea, Christmas is a big couple's day.

items.exampleKo: About what time do you arrive?
I just left, I'll be there soon.
I'm running a bit late because of work.
Go ahead first, I'll come later.
Come pick me up at the station.
Do you want to stay over tonight?
Let's make a travel plan.
Ready? Let's head out.
By the way, are you free tomorrow?
items.tip: Casual form of 그런데.

items.exampleKo: It's raining so I'm staying home.

items.example: 먼저 밥 먹고, 그리고 영화 보자.
items.exampleKo: Let's eat first, and then watch a movie.
By the way, what did you do yesterday?
Actually, I have something to say.
For example, what kind of movies do you like?
In the end, I stayed home.
Let's eat first.
After that, we watched a movie.
It's cheap and also delicious.
I'm tired. I'll go anyway.
Anyway, let's meet and talk.
Honestly, I'm a bit tired.
It'll probably be fine.
Let's definitely come again.
If you have time, call me.
I want to go, but I'm busy.
items.tip: A very common ending that sets up a contrast or background.

items.exampleKo: It's late, so I'm going to bed.
Text me when you arrive.
Call me when you're lonely.
It suddenly started raining.
I'll reply right away.
My Korean is gradually improving.
We finally met.
You haven't slept yet?
I already arrived.
I just got home.
I've been waiting this whole time.
I go to that shop often.

items.example: 술 한 번도 안 마셔 봤어.
items.exampleKo: I've never had a drink.
We're almost there.
I especially like this place.
I'm a little tired.
I miss you so much.
items.tip: Means "too much", but Koreans use it for "so" in a good way too.

items.exampleKo: Eat a lot.
I arrived earlier.
I'll call you later.
items.tip: Used only for later the same day.

items.exampleKo: Let's go together sometime.
Oh no, I lost my phone!
I left my wallet at home.
My phone battery is almost dead.
I missed the last train.
There's traffic, so I'll be late.
I caught a cold.
I have a bit of a fever.
I've had a headache since morning.
My stomach hurts so I can't move.
You should see a doctor.
